topics.title: Investment in Debt Securities
topics.summary: Classification, recognition, measurement, amortization, and fair value treatment of debt securities.
topics.discussion: Debt securities are financial assets that represent a contractual right to receive cash, such as bonds. Under IFRS 9, debt securities may be classified depending on the entity's business model and the contractual cash flow characteristics of the instrument. Common classifications include amortized cost, fair value through other comprehensive income, and fair value through profit or loss.
topics.formula: Amortized Cost = Initial Carrying Amount + Interest Income - Cash Received ± Amortization
topics.computation: Example: A bond is acquired for ₱950,000 with a face value of ₱1,000,000. If the effective interest method is used, the discount is amortized over the life of the bond and increases the carrying amount until maturity.

topics.title: Inventories
topics.summary: Recognition, measurement, inventory cost, net realizable value, and cost formulas.
topics.discussion: Inventories are assets held for sale in the ordinary course of business, in the process of production for sale, or in the form of materials or supplies to be consumed in production. Under PAS 2, inventories are measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value.
topics.formula: Inventory Value = Lower of Cost and Net Realizable Value
topics.computation: Example: If inventory cost is ₱120,000 and net realizable value is ₱100,000, the inventory should be reported at ₱100,000. A write-down of ₱20,000 is recognized as expense.

topics.title: Property, Plant and Equipment
topics.summary: Recognition, initial cost, depreciation, revaluation, impairment, and disposal.
topics.discussion: Property, plant and equipment are tangible assets held for use in production, supply of goods or services, rental to others, or administrative purposes and are expected to be used for more than one period. Under PAS 16, an item of PPE is recognized when future economic benefits are probable and the cost can be measured reliably.
topics.computation: Example: Equipment costs ₱500,000, has a residual value of ₱50,000, and useful life of 5 years. Annual depreciation is (₱500,000 - ₱50,000) ÷ 5 = ₱90,000.

quizBank.question: Under PAS 2, inventories are measured at:
quizBank.explanation: PAS 2 requires inventories to be measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value.
